video_title: KidSuper on Fashion, Creativity & Building a Brand | Off Script w/ Trip Ep. 6

quotes.speaker: Colm Dillane
quotes.summary_phrase: Colm Dillane on clothing as a cape for superheroes
quotes.excerpt: I like this idea of clothing being a cape that you wear before you go do superhero stuff.

text_blocks.speaker: Jaren Jackson Jr.
text_blocks.text: When did you stop realizing it wasn't just outfits you were making? You're making memories for people, you're making experiences.

text_blocks.speaker: Colm Dillane
text_blocks.text: I like this idea of clothing being a cape that you wear before you go do superhero stuff. Putting on an outfit and making you feel better or like you can fly. Now sometimes athletes wear it before games, and they play amazing. It's obviously because of the clothes that I made. We've had some moments where before Super Bowl Travis Kelce wore it and won. We had some with soccer players. Neymar just wore the cleats in the World Cup, and he scored a goal that I got to witness live in cleats that said KidSuper.

quotes.speaker: Colm Dillane
quotes.summary_phrase: Colm Dillane on the inspiration behind the KidSuper runway show
quotes.excerpt: I wanted to be the brand that represented soccer the most true.

text_blocks.speaker: Jaren Jackson Jr.
text_blocks.text: You even did a show at a stadium, which is crazy. Having the models come out with the kids, you not just using it as a venue, but you meshed it together to keep it true to it.

text_blocks.speaker: Colm Dillane
text_blocks.text: I wanted to be the brand that represented soccer the most true. A lot of brands now are doing quick jersey collabs for the World Cup. I was like, no, we're the real soccer brand. I got this opportunity to do it at Inter Miami's stadium. We got the crazy stadium and then Sean Paul, which if you know anything about me, if I'm at a party, I'll usually go up to the DJ and be like, you're fucking this up, just play Sean Paul. And that's all I want to listen to.

quotes.speaker: Colm Dillane
quotes.summary_phrase: Colm Dillane on the core philosophy of the KidSuper brand
quotes.excerpt: I felt it was based more on this mind state of being open and optimistic.

text_blocks.speaker: Jaren Jackson Jr.
text_blocks.text: After seeing so much of your work that just scratches the surface of what you are, I want to know in your words, what is KidSuper?

text_blocks.speaker: Colm Dillane
text_blocks.text: For me, obviously fashion design is the catalyst to enter everything. When I was creating the brand, I felt it was based more on this mind state of being open and optimistic, this childlike sense of wonder and ambitious, and a little bit mischievous as children are. I was truly a KidSuper character. I wanted to be the brand that represented soccer the most true. Is KidSuper football club possible? Is KidSuper food truck possible? Is KidSuper media possible? I loved that it all felt part of the one umbrella.

quotes.speaker: Colm Dillane
quotes.summary_phrase: Colm Dillane on using comedy in fashion runway shows
quotes.excerpt: I don't delete any of my Instagram pictures because I need a record of people.

text_blocks.speaker: Colm Dillane
text_blocks.text: I don't delete any of my Instagram pictures because I need a record of people to be like, no, I, for example, we did a comedy fashion show, which was quite cool, where we had comedians walk and come out and do jokes. Someone was like, oh, you're on comedy now? And if you scroll down my Instagram seven years ago, I tried to do comedy shows out of my old store. So comedy has always been a huge part of the KidSuper brand.

quotes.speaker: Colm Dillane
quotes.summary_phrase: Colm Dillane on the 'runners fast as you can' show concept
quotes.excerpt: I didn't realize I created a human slip and slide.

text_blocks.speaker: Colm Dillane
text_blocks.text: I did this fashion show where the models stepped on paint and walked around this cube video, and the last model was in a white suit and he was a break dancer. He would break dance on the floor, and I would have a path of all the painting footsteps. An hour before the show, the venue was like, you can't put paint on the ground. I was like, this is my whole concept. What if I cover everything in plastic, is that okay? I didn't realize I created a human slip and slide. The models stepped on paint, walked, and slipped.

quotes.speaker: Colm Dillane
quotes.summary_phrase: Colm Dillane on the importance of the show's closing speech
quotes.excerpt: Sometimes you slip and fall, but you have to remember to get up and run.

text_blocks.speaker: Colm Dillane
text_blocks.text: As I came out at the end, I said, sometimes you slip and fall, but you have to remember to get up and run as fast as you can. The show was called Runners Fast As You Can. Because of that, the Vogue writer came up to me and was like, the fact that you had the model slip was so brilliant and really pushed the idea forward.

quotes.speaker: Colm Dillane
quotes.summary_phrase: Colm Dillane on the Bape collaboration and packaging
quotes.excerpt: Bape was obviously the OG streetwear brand, but they were kind of one of the first.

text_blocks.speaker: Colm Dillane
text_blocks.text: Bape was obviously the OG streetwear brand, but they were kind of one of the first streetwear brands to really care about packaging because they came from the Japanese lens. The Japanese are really, really focused on detail, attention-driven, and they cared about stuff that maybe American brands weren't caring about at the time, like the packaging, like the experience. And so when I got the honor of doing a Bape collab, I was like, even before we did the shoe, I was like, the packaging has to be incredible.

quotes.speaker: Colm Dillane
quotes.summary_phrase: Colm Dillane on his problem-solving approach to design
quotes.excerpt: I think people often ask how ideas come to KidSuper and for me it's all problem solving.

text_blocks.speaker: Colm Dillane
text_blocks.text: I think people often ask how ideas come to KidSuper and for me it's all problem solving. Okay, you have 48 different countries. How do you represent all of them within a photoshoot? How do you and then you're like, okay, who represents what country? Okay, you get an athlete from one and then so then I was kept going, I was like, man, what's like unanimous across all these countries? And grandmas, and then New York City is a beautiful place because everyone immigrates here. So then I could find 48 grandmothers.

quotes.speaker: Colm Dillane
quotes.summary_phrase: Colm Dillane on the KidSuper theater play runway show
quotes.excerpt: I had to direct him and it was very funny because I was so shy with it.

text_blocks.speaker: Colm Dillane
text_blocks.text: The one you saw, which was the theater play, like we always wanted to put on a theater play. And I'm in it, which was insane. And that has like the craziest backstory of a story to get to where that is. But then the the most recent one, the soccer stadium, what a dream. And that's like something I always wanted to experience. Sean Paul is like my favorite artist, if you ask everyone. I've been trying to book him for like 10 years. And then the one before that was a short film with Vincent Cassel, which La Haine is one of my favorite movies and getting to be work with him and I had to direct him and it was very funny because I was so shy with it.

quotes.speaker: Colm Dillane
quotes.summary_phrase: Colm Dillane on the importance of finishing products
quotes.excerpt: The main thing is become the person amongst your friends that is known for finishing things.

text_blocks.speaker: Jaren Jackson Jr.
text_blocks.text: What advice would you give to someone who looks up to you and wants to do what you've done?

text_blocks.speaker: Colm Dillane
text_blocks.text: I think the main thing is become the person amongst your friends that is known for finishing things. You don't have to be the best, you don't have to be the worst, but if you're a guy that's like every month finishing a product, releasing a product, you will inspire people around you because they'll be like, that's a guy who shows up and you're going to get better because you're learning and making stuff, but do not be a flake.
